text:
elena: Heads-up — digging into GCP KMS boundaries for Private deployments. We want runtime nodes in customer VPC (project-a) to unwrap envelope keys, but store the primary CryptoKey in a central security project (project-secrets). What's a secure SA/delegation + audit pattern that minimizes blast radius?

samir: We implemented a similar pattern last quarter. High-level: keep the CryptoKey in project-secrets, own it with a dedicated SA (kms-decrypt@project-secrets). Give that SA key-level role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter. Then let the runner SA in project-a impersonate the kms-decrypt SA instead of granting direct key access.

samir: Typical bindings:
```
# allow runner SA to impersonate the central SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding kms-decrypt@project-secrets.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="serviceAccount:runner@project-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

# grant the central SA only the key-level role (narrow scope)
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-key \
  --location=global --keyring=prod-ring \
  --member="serviceAccount:kms-decrypt@project-secrets.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```

samir: This keeps the key owner isolated and auditable in project-secrets. The runtime in project-a requests short-lived tokens from STS to impersonate kms-decrypt and calls KMS. No long-lived cross-project key bindings. :lock:

kai: Additional notes: enable Cloud Audit Logs for both Admin and Data Access on project-secrets (cloudkms.googleapis.com). Export decrypt/crypto operations to a sink (BigQuery or LogBucket) for retention and forensic queries. Without Data Access logs you won't see actual cryptographic operations.

kai: For envelope encryption, only the unwrap operation (decrypt) needs to be logged. Make sure the runtime records a local audit event too (what envelope ID, which model ID, request id). Correlate logs via trace/request-id.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Reminder: rotation policy. Rotate key versions regularly (e.g., 90d) and run an automated rewrap job that re-encrypts stored envelope keys under the new primary. Keep previous versions for a grace window (30–90d) for rollback. If crypto service is unreachable, fall back to short-lived cached envelope keys in a hardware-backed ephemeral store, not long-term.

anna_devex: Operational/config items for Private deployments: ensure VPC egress rules allow KMS endpoints (or use Private Service Connect). KMS traffic must route to the public KMS endpoints unless you use Private Service Connect + peering to the Google service. Also validate DNS/firewall so the runner can reach oauth2 and iam endpoints for impersonation token exchange.

nick_sre: Quick checklist we used: 
1) Create central SA scoped to key ring.
2) Bind only roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter at key level.
3) Grant runner SA roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the central SA (scoped).
4) Enable Data Access audit logs for cloudkms.googleapis.com in project-secrets and export.
5) Set up rewrap/rekey job, monitor failures, and alert.
6) Use IAM Conditions where possible (e.g., restrict impersonation to specific member or workload identity pool).

nick_sre: Example: using IAM Conditions to restrict impersonation to a workload identity pool: 
```
# pseudo: add condition so only runner pool can impersonate
# condition: request.auth.claims.aud == "//iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_A/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL"
```

elena: Quick Q — token lifetime: when runner impersonates kms-decrypt SA, what's safe for token TTL? We want short-lived but not too chatty.

samir: Use token exchange + set TTL to low values (1–5m) for crypto ops. The fewer seconds the token is valid, the smaller the window for misuse. Implement local caching of tokens for a tiny window to avoid high QPS to the TokenCreator endpoint.

elena: Any gotchas for envelope key caching? We plan to cache unwrapped envelope keys in memory only and never persist. Ops concerns about node restarts though.

kai: That’s right — keep them in memory (sealed) and rotate frequently. If you must persist (e.g., for graceful shutdown), encrypt with instance-local KMS (or use ephemeral HSM) and have short TTL. Also ensure crash dumps don't include keys.

elena: Sounds good. I'll draft a runbook: SA creation, key-level bindings, audit sink steps, rotation cadence, and fallback cache rules. Tagging @samir @kai @nick_sre for review. Thanks all :raised_hands:

samir: happy to review. Also suggest adding an alert on IAM policy changes to the central SA and key IAM bindings (notify security-oncall).
